newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus knows no Boeing pressure on U.S. suppliers.
newsitem.headline: Airbus knows no Boeing pressure on U.S. suppliers.

text.p: European aircraft consortium Airbus Industrie said Friday that it had no evidence that archrival Boeing Co. was putting pressure on U.S. suppliers to prevent them from working on Airbus' planned super-jumbo jetliner.

Newspapers quoted Daimler-Benz Aerospace Chairman Manfred Bischoff as saying Thursday that he was concerned Boeing and merger partner McDonnell Douglas Corp. were trying to induce a big U.S. subcontractor -- understood to be Northrop Grumman Corp. -- not to work on the Airbus project.
"We have no evidence of any kind of pressure," an Airbus spokesman said.

However, an industry source close to Airbus said Boeing had put pressure on Northrop to stay out of the so-called A3XX project, which threatens Boeing's lucrative monopoly in the high-capacity aircraft segment with its 747 jumbo.
"It is a fact," the source said.
Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a subsidiary of Daimler-Benz AG of Germany, is a partner in Airbus Industrie along with France's Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc and Casa of Spain.
Officials of Seattle-based Boeing were not immediately available to comment.
Airbus had been in exploratory talks with Northrop over supplying engine housing sections for the A3XX, but those negotiations had ended, the industry source said.

The European consortium has been looking for risk-sharing partners to supply up to 40 percent of the targeted $8 billion in the A3XX development costs. The plane would seat 550 passengers in the basic version.
